negative_results: THE LEVER ITSELF. The prefetch does issue round n+1's loads before round n's mma, and it is bit-identical -- but one KC=2 round is 8 mma plus L1/L2-resident A loads, a few hundred cycles against a ~600-cycle miss, so it hides only part of the latency and pays a second live register array for the rest.

A FOUR-register increase (64 -> 68) cost up to 38.5% in the bench because at 256 threads it is the 4 -> 3 blocks/SM step. Restoring the occupancy with __launch_bounds__ recovered 35 of those points. Trap 21.

__launch_bounds__(T,1) on the SHARED template took the DB=false instantiation from 64 to 84 registers -- minBlocks=1 stops ptxas economising -- which would have silently changed the control arm of this A/B. Split into a __device__ body plus two __global__ entries. Trap 22.

The only shapes DB helps are W=4 (sw1/3, -7.2%) and W=1 (wkv, -3.2%), which are the shared expert and wkv -- both already forked to a side stream and hidden by F55, which is why nothing reaches the end-to-end number.

pivot_criterion.why: S5 (draft-head re-alignment) is a TRAINING job the autonomous loop cannot do. Kernel work and training compete for the same operator attention, so the loop must say plainly when kernel work has stopped paying rather than grinding sub-1% levers forever.
pivot_criterion.trigger: PIVOT when open_nontraining_levers == 0 on TWO consecutive audits, OR when three consecutive cycles adopt nothing >=1%. Either fires -> the auditor writes a PIVOT banner to FLYWHEEL_AUDIT.md and creates FLYWHEEL_PIVOT.
